Oral Order 05/Dated: 15.02.2024 Heard the counsel for the parties.

The petitioner has prayed for a direction upon the respondents to pay the amount of compensation in lieu of acquisition of land which was acquired for widening and construction of four lane Ranchi- Gumla National Highway Road.

It is the case of the petitioner that the land belongs to this petitioner and his ancestors but the same was acquired by the National Highway Authority, yet, till date, the amount of compensation has not been paid.
Learned counsel for the State submits that there was some conflict raised by the co-sharers, thus, an enquiry was conducted and a report has already been submitted.
Admittedly, the land has been acquired under the National Highway Act of 1986.
The detailed procedure has been prescribed in the aforesaid Act as to how the compensation has to be paid.

Section 3 H of the Act reads as follows:-

sentences.text: Deposit and payment of amount.--(1) The amount determined under section 3G shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner asmay be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.

(2) As soon as may be after the amount has been deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

(3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

(5) Where the amount determined under section 3G by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the arbitrator may award interest at nine per cent, per annum on such excess amount from the date of taking possession under section 3D till the date of the actual deposit thereof.

(6)Where the amount determined by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the excess amount together with interest, if any, awarded under sub-section (5) shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government,
with the competent authority and the provisions of subsections (2) to (4) shall apply to such deposit."
Thus, the State has to take a decision in respect of payment of compensation and who is to receive the same.
Admittedly, no amount of compensation has been paid to any person in relation to acquisition of the land, which is the subject matter of this writ application.

Thus, I direct the Competent Authority to take appropriate decision in this matter and decide as to who is entitled to receive the amount of compensation and ensure that the amount of compensation is paid at the earliest, preferably within a period of four months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, this writ petition stands disposed of.
